bio: FamilySearch credits Matthew Scott (b. Sunderland, Mass., 21 Aug 1739) with a run of Vermont militia service from 1764 to 1782, including Revolutionary War rolls, and places him in Bennington in the 1790 census ([R4-S1]). If he were Johnny's ancestor this would be a second Revolutionary patriot line. But the chain to Johnny is weak: it runs through Daniel Scott (whom FamilySearch has born in 1788, making him Matthew's youngest son) to Stephen J. Scott (b. 1806), and neither link has a document. The 1810 Pittston household of 'Daniel Scott Jr.' (a man aged 26-44) does not fit a Daniel born in 1788, and the 'Jr.' points to an older Daniel Scott in the Wyoming Valley rather than to a Vermont father (see Daniel Scott jr). Treat Matthew as unverified.

residences.place: Bennington, VT (1790 census 'Mathew Scott', per FamilySearch)

military.note: FamilySearch lists thirteen Vermont military-service events 1764-1782 (1778-82 during the Revolution, incl. Bennington and Windham) and attaches a 'United States Revolutionary War Rolls, 1775-1783' entry for Mathew Scott (index ark 1:1:QL65-VGD2). Not checked against the roll images; possible Revolutionary service. [R4-S1]

openQuestions: Before any SAR use: prove Daniel Scott (father of Stephen) was Matthew's son; the Bennington 1790 household and Vermont records of a son Daniel would be needed.
